question: What are the main causes of negative sentiment, and what specifically triggers them?

answer.answer_markdown:
**The biggest cause of negative sentiment is not the original problem but a decision the customer cannot get explained or overturned - "denied or declined without explanation" sits behind 21.6% of contacts, more than any other driver.**

The mood is bad almost everywhere: 61.6% of contacts carry mild negative sentiment and a further 23.5% are strongly negative, and 74.2% end unresolved. The causes behind that are failures of handling rather than of product. After decisions denied or declined without explanation (21.6%) come fraud that was not stopped or not refunded (19.4%), incorrect or conflicting information (15.1%) and money held or not returned (13.4%), then errors that were never corrected (9.8%) and a plain failure to respond or follow up (8.5%).

The specific triggers are concrete and repetitive. The largest single theme is unexplained account closures and restrictions (7.5% of contacts), where risk models restrict or close an account - often right after a large deposit or a fraud flag - and policy stops agents from saying why. It is concentrated in everyday checking and savings (12.8%, about 1.71 times the overall rate), and customers describe a 10-day closure notice with no reason given, 16-year and 20-year-old accounts closed without warning, and being refused any new account after their own were compromised. Next come fraud and dispute claims denied despite evidence (7.3%) - ATM claims closed without reconciling the cash cassettes or pulling the footage, disputes rejected under a misapplied deadline rule - and contradictory information from representatives (7.1%), where the story changes between departments and between calls.

The angriest contacts are not the fraud ones. Measured by average sentiment, customer service experience is the worst of the large reasons (-1.43), worse than unauthorized activity or fraud (-1.26), while terms, information or communication is the mildest (-0.25). The fraud, the hold or the denial starts the complaint; what makes it bitter is the handling afterwards - repeated transfers, shifting explanations, and nobody who is allowed to say why.

caveats: The index holds two different corpora: the bulk is real written complaints about one bank covering July 2024 to June 2026, and the rest is a set of synthetic agent/customer phone conversations from a single month in September 2023. The figures here are unfiltered and mix the two.

The negative skew is largely a property of the source. Almost all of the positive sentiment in the index comes from the synthetic conversations, because a complaint corpus contains very little of it, so this is not evidence that customers became unhappier - it is what a complaint file looks like.

For the same reason, terms, information or communication scores far milder than the other reasons: most of those contacts are ordinary enquiries from the synthetic conversations rather than complaints.
Driver categories and themes are assigned per topic and one contact can carry several, so these groups overlap and their counts do not sum to the contact total.
followups: Where risk closes or restricts an account, how much of the anger is the decision itself versus the refusal to give a reason - and what could be disclosed without breaching the policy?
Denied fraud and dispute claims are a top driver: what share of denials are later reversed on appeal, and what evidence was missed the first time?

confidence.badge: broad pattern · 4,511 calls · 25 months · 10 products · 53 states
